chunks: Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Sa'id al-Hashimi al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Furat b. Ibrahim b. Furat al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ali al-Hamadani narrated to me. He said: Al-Husayn b. Ali narrated to me. He said: Abdullah b. Sa'id al-Hashimi narrated to me. He said: Abd al-Wahid b. Ghiyath narrated to me. He said: Asim b. Sulayman narrated to us. He said: Juwaybir narrated to us from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. He said:

We prayed the final Isha prayer one night with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family. When he recited the taslim, he turned his face toward us, then said: Verily, a meteor will fall from the sky at the rise of dawn and land in the house of one of you. Whoever has that meteor fall in his house, then he is my deputy, my vicegerent, and the Imam after me.

When dawn drew near, every one of us sat in his house waiting for the meteor to fall in his house. The most desirous of the people for that was my father, al-Abbas b. Abd al-Muttalib. When dawn broke, the meteor fell from the air and landed in the house of Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said to Ali, peace be upon him: O Ali, by Him who raised me with prophethood, the deputyship, the vicegerency, and the Imamate have been obligated for you after me.

Then the hypocrites, Abdullah b. Ubay and his companions, said: Muhammad has deviated in his love for his cousin and gone astray, and he only speaks about him out of desire. So God, blessed and exalted, revealed: 'By the star when it fades away' — God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: By the Creator of the star when it fades away — 'Your companion has not deviated' — meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and his family, in his love for Ali b. Abi Talib — 'nor has he gone astray. Nor does he speak out of desire' — meaning, with regards to him — 'It is not but a revealed revelation.'

key_terms.الإمامة: Imamate — divinely appointed leadership of the Muslim community
key_terms.المنافقون: The hypocrites — a Quranic term for those who feigned belief while opposing Islam
key_terms.الوصية: Deputyship (wasiyya) — the testamentary designation of a successor
key_terms.وحي يوحى: A revealed revelation — indicating divine origin of the Prophet's words about Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of Surah al-Najm (53:1-4) regarding the succession of Ali b. Abi Talib?
ai.summary: Ibn Abbas narrates that after praying the final Isha prayer with the Prophet, the Prophet predicted a meteor would fall at dawn into the house of his true successor. Al-Abbas b. Abd al-Muttalib was the most eager, but the meteor fell in Ali's house. When the hypocrites led by Abdullah b. Ubay accused the Prophet of favoritism, God revealed the opening verses of Surah al-Najm (53:1-4) to vindicate him, explaining that his appointment of Ali was by divine revelation, not personal desire.
